title: The organization of visual pathways in the Drosophila brain.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the public MaleCNS v1.0 flat-connectome bucket (no login): annotations 14.5 MB, neurotransmitter predictions 43 MB, connection weights 0.50-1.05 GB, synapse partners 3-6.8 GB, synapse points 13 GB. Downloaded and opened the annotations feather: 211,577 bodies x 36 columns; 164,506 have a cell type (11,751 types, 3,619 types with >=5 neurons); 105,265 bodies are optic-lobe or visual-projection classes (736 types). Lineage columns: itoleeHl 37,754 rows/203 values, trumanHl 19,753/76; birthtime 7,904 rows but only 13 'late'.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Paper is paywalled with no Europe PMC full text; I read only the abstract and search snippets of the bioRxiv preprint (10.64898/2025.12.22.696097). The paper's pathway classes, predicted receptive fields and feature biases, and the physiological comparison set, were not seen in any file; I do not know if they are deposited as tables.

a1_downloadable.note: Flat connectome files are in a public Google Cloud bucket, checked by listing. neuPrint's API needs a free account token, but the bulk files do not.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The paper's outputs (pathway class, predicted receptive field, input mixture per neuron type) are not columns in the released files I opened; they would have to be rebuilt from the paper's network analysis. Cell type is a column (164,506 typed bodies, checked).

a3_inputs_present.note: Connectivity weights keyed by bodyId are present (file sizes checked, contents not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: Weights are synapse counts; soma locations are in 8 nm voxels per the download page.

a5_enough_rows.note: The only measured (non-connectome) label for visual function is physiology for a few dozen cell types, per the abstract and prior literature; count not verified, but far below 400.

a6_fits_laptop.note: An optic-lobe subgraph fits in 16 GB; synapse-level files (3-13 GB) are not needed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checked against the paper's neuron counts (no full text); the annotation file parsed cleanly.

a8_label_provenance.note: Circular in every version of the task: the paper's receptive-field and pathway labels are computed from the connectome itself; cell types were assigned largely from connectivity and morphology; neurotransmitter identity is a neural-network prediction from EM images.

existing_models.name: Connectome-constrained deep mechanistic networks (Lappalainen et al., Nature 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicted direction selectivity and ON/OFF polarity for optic-lobe cell types, checked against published physiology for tens of types; scores not retrieved.

existing_models.name: Predicting visual function by interpreting a neuronal wiring diagram (Seung lab, Nature 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Receptive-field and orientation predictions from FlyWire connectivity; numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: This paper's network signal-propagation analysis (male CNS connectome)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicted receptive fields and feature biases said to agree with physiological data; numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: None standard; no open pretrained connectome foundation model of the ESM-2 kind
backbone.hardware: CPU is enough for graph features or node2vec-style embeddings
backbone.licence: Janelia FlyEM data is released openly (exact licence not checked)

integration.join_key: flywireType column (143,156 bodies carry one, checked)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a wiring-to-function mapping learned in one fly brain transfer to another fly of the other sex?

controls.positive_control: Recover ON/OFF split and T4/T5 direction selectivity from connectivity
controls.negative_control: Shuffle cell-type labels on the graph
controls.external_validation: FlyWire connectome; published calcium-imaging physiology for tens of cell types

honest_claim_h3: Any model would reproduce connectivity-derived annotations from connectivity, or predict physiology for only a few dozen measured cell types, not learn visual function from independent measurements.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a neuron's wiring in the fly brain to predict what visual feature it responds to.
plain_idea.train_on: Synapse-count connections for 105,265 optic-lobe and visual-projection neurons in 736 types (checked), summarised per neuron type.
plain_idea.predict: Visual response properties such as light-on versus light-off preference or motion direction, whose true values come from calcium-imaging recordings for only a few dozen types (count unknown).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Visual neuroscientists could prioritise which of thousands of unrecorded cell types to image; but the labels are too few, and the paper's own predictions come from the same wiring.

more_or_better_data.why: The male CNS connectome adds a second complete brain to FlyWire, but the measured physiology labels are the same few dozen cell types that the 2024 Nature models already used.

confidence_score.why: There is one animal per connectome and no repeated physiology at scale, so per-prediction noise cannot be estimated.

models_beatable.why: The 2024 connectome-constrained networks are recent, open and mechanistic; beating them on tens of labelled types would not be statistically meaningful.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new independent physiology measurements join to this data; adding a second connectome supplies more features, not more labels.

ml_idea: Predict physiological feature selectivity of visual neuron types from connectivity; rejected because labels are either connectome-derived (circular) or physiology for only tens of types. Side note for a separate MaleCNS resource evaluation: the itoleeHl developmental-lineage column (37,754 neurons, 203 values, checked) is assigned from neurite tracts, not wiring, and could be a less circular target for a wiring-predicts-lineage project.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes in the bucket listing; nothing was timed beyond opening the 14 MB annotation file.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count cell types with published physiological feature labels that match MaleCNS types; under ~400 kills it (expected tens).

verdict_reason: Fails A8 and A5: the paper's pathway and receptive-field labels are computed from the connectome itself, cell types are defined mostly from connectivity, and the independent physiological ground truth covers only a few dozen cell types. The data itself is public and model-ready, so it is better judged under a MaleCNS resource paper.
